descriptionAdvanced.en: Dalian, located at the southern tip of the Liaodong Peninsula, is a major port city in Northeast China, distinguished by its unique architecture and scenic coastal landscapes. The city's relatively brief but eventful history was significantly shaped by Russian and Japanese influences during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Originally founded as the Russian commercial port of Dalny, it later flourished under Japanese administration following the Russo-Japanese War before returning to Chinese control in 1945. These historical layers are still evident in the city's grand public squares, such as Zhongshan Square, and its distinctive Russian-style districts. Today, Dalian is recognized as one of the most dynamic financial and logistics hubs in the Bohai Rim region, celebrated for its high standard of living and urban green spaces. Beyond its industrial prowess, tourism thrives as millions visit its numerous beaches and coastal parks annually. As a frequent host of the 'Summer Davos,' Dalian solidifies its standing as an internationally significant modern economic center.

en: Dalian features Xinghai Square, one of the largest public city squares in the world (1.1 million mÂ²).
The city was established by Russia in 1898 as a strategic ice-free port named Dalny.
Dalian is a major national hub for shipbuilding and the IT outsourcing (ITO) industry.
The Binhai Road stretches 32 kilometers along the city's scenic southern coastline.
In 1984, Dalian was designated as one of the first 14 coastal cities to open to foreign trade.
The city alternates as the host of the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions.
